description: The plot illustrates how Mean Reciprocal Rank at 10 (MRR@10) varies with different query selection strategies for Dense Passage Retrieval (DPR) as the number of queries used during inference changes. The x-axis is labeled “Number of queries used during inference (S)” on a linear scale, spanning 1 to 10 with integer tick marks. The y-axis is labeled “MRR@10” on a linear scale, ranging from 33.0 to 36.5 with ticks every 0.5. A black solid horizontal line (“DPR w/o query”) stays constant at about 34.25 across all S. A yellow solid line with circular markers (“DPR w/ gold”) appears from S=4 to S=10 and increases from about 33.0 at S=4 to about 34.95 at S=10, rising at each step (e.g., ~33.35 at S=5, ~33.8 at S=6, ~34.1 at S=7, ~34.5 at S=8, ~34.75 at S=9). A green solid line with circular markers (“DPR w/ top-1”) starts near 33.0 at S=1 and increases throughout to about 36.4 at S=10, with intermediate points around ~34.7 (S=2), ~35.1 (S=3), ~35.45 (S=4), ~35.7 (S=5), ~35.85 (S=6), ~36.1 (S=7), ~36.2 (S=8), and ~36.33 (S=9). A purple solid line with circular markers (“DPR w/ bottom-1”) fluctuates slightly but trends downward overall, moving from about 34.75 at S=1 to about 34.7 at S=10, with values around ~34.9 (S=2), ~35.05 (S=3), ~34.88 (S=4), ~34.82 (S=5), ~34.88 (S=6), ~34.8 (S=7), ~34.72 (S=8), and ~34.75 (S=9). A blue solid line with circular markers (“DPR w/ random”) rises early and then stays near 35.2–35.3, going from about 34.75 at S=1 to about 35.3 at S=10, with points around ~35.15 (S=2), ~35.28 (S=3), ~35.3 (S=4), ~35.22 (S=5), ~35.25 (S=6), ~35.22 (S=7), ~35.22 (S=8), and ~35.23 (S=9). A red solid line with circular markers (“DPR w/ curriculum”) increases from about 35.15 at S=1 to about 35.78 at S=10, with values near ~35.55 (S=2), ~35.58 (S=3), ~35.68 (S=4), ~35.72 (S=5), ~35.77 (S=6), ~35.8 (S=7), ~35.75 (S=8), and ~35.8 (S=9). Three dashed horizontal reference lines are also shown: a red dashed line at about 35.6, a purple dashed line at about 34.9, and a green dashed line at about 34.65.
caption_used: Comparison of query selection strategies in Dense Passage Retrieval (DPR) evaluated via Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR@10) on the MS-Marco development set. The x-axis denotes the number of queries used during inference (S), ranging from 2 to 10, while the y-axis represents MRR@10, spanning from 33.0 to 36.5. Six strategies are depicted: DPR without query expansion (black solid line, constant at approximately 34.3), DPR with curriculum-based query selection (red solid line with circles, rising modestly from 35.1 to 35.8), DPR with top-1 query selection (green solid line with triangles, increasing sharply from 33.0 to 36.5), DPR with random query selection (blue solid line with circles, stabilizing around 34.5 after an initial rise), DPR with bottom-1 query selection (purple solid line with circles, declining steadily from 35.2 to 34.6), and DPR with gold query selection (yellow solid line with circles, surging from 33.0 at S=4 to 35.0 at S=10). Dashed lines represent typical DPR representations without corpus expansion, with the red dashed line (curriculum) consistently outperforming others at 35.6, while the green dashed line (top-1) plateaus at 34.2. Notably, the DPR with random queries initially surpasses the curriculum-based approach but is subsequently overtaken as the number of queries increases. The gold query strategy demonstrates the most rapid improvement, though it fails to match the peak performance of the top-1 strategy by S=10. These results suggest that while targeted query selection strategies (e.g., top-1) yield the highest MRR gains, even suboptimal strategies like bottom-1 can maintain competitive performance under limited query conditions.
